identity.title: Characterizing, Evaluating, and Optimizing Complex Reasoning

problem.claim: The paper addresses how to characterize, evaluate, and optimize complex reasoning traces used by Large Reasoning Models.

gap.claim: Existing work lacks a unified answer about reasoning quality, reliable evaluation of long implicitly structured traces, and use of evaluation signals for optimization.

contributions.claim: Introduces the ME² principle, characterizing reasoning quality at macro and micro levels through efficiency and effectiveness.
Models reasoning traces as directed acyclic graphs and develops a DAG-based pairwise evaluator, then trains a Thinking Reward Model using the TRM-Preference dataset.
Provides the TRM-Preference dataset, Thinking Reward Model, and associated code and data.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present a unified perspective connecting quality characterization, DAG-based evaluation, and reasoning optimization.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that, at test time, selecting better reasoning improves outcomes by up to 19.3% across diverse tasks.
The authors report that, during reinforcement-learning training, thinking rewards enhance reasoning and performance by up to 3.9% across diverse tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Large Reasoning Models increasingly use reasoning traces with complex internal structures.
The abstract identifies three unresolved needs: defining quality, evaluating long implicit structures, and using evaluation for optimization.
The paper proposes the ME² principle and represents traces as DAGs for pairwise evaluation.
The approach yields the TRM-Preference dataset and TRM; reported gains occur in test-time selection and RL training.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns a quality principle, a structured evaluation representation, a reward model, and two optimization settings.

lessons.interpretation: A tightly linked chain can make a broad reasoning agenda more concrete and traceable.
lessons.application: Frame a reasoning paper by mapping each conceptual quality dimension to an evaluator and then to a specific optimization use case.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the work addresses only one isolated component or lacks evidence for downstream use.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the ME² dimensions beyond efficiency and effectiveness, the DAG construction, evaluation protocol, baselines, task identities, or statistical details.
The reported percentage gains lack denominators, datasets, and uncertainty information in the supplied units.
